02 / The idea, without the mystery
①

Keep something private.

Alice and Bob each choose a private number, X. It stays with its owner. The public numbers q and α are the same for everyone.

②

Share something public.

Each calculates Y = αX mod q and sends Y across the open channel. With properly chosen, large parameters, reversing this is difficult.

③

Meet at the same secret.

Raise the received Y to your own private X, modulo q. Both arrive at αXA × XB mod q. The secret itself never travels.

⌁

But who’s on the other end?

Basic Diffie–Hellman doesn’t verify identity. An active attacker can replace public keys and agree on a secret with each person. Authenticate the exchange with verified signatures and certificates to prevent this.
